newsitem.title: UK: 11 pct of 1997 UK wool clip sold pre-season - board.
newsitem.headline: 11 pct of 1997 UK wool clip sold pre-season - board.

text.p: The British Wool Marketing Board (BWMB) aims to start the 1997 selling season with 11 percent of the clip sold and no stockpile from the 1996 season, Managing Director Ian Hartley said.
"We are well on our way to achieving our overall objective of getting ahead of the market," he said in a report on the Board's annual conference, held on November 1.
The BWMB projected that 60 percent of the current 46.5 million kg clip would be sold by the end of December 1996, compared to 48 percent the previous year.
The UK wool season runs from around June-June and the current year's clip is sheared in August.
"We plan to increase the amount of wool sold forward, thus starting the 1997 season with significantly reduced levels of its clip to sell," Hartley said.
The BWMB offers four forward-unavailable contracts (offered one, three, six and nine months ahead), which enables buyers to secure a consignment of wool while it is still on the sheep's back.
"During the period January-June 1997 we are planning to offer over five million kg of wool compared to the 1.9 and 1.8 million kg offered the previous two years," Hartley said.
"We would then be going into the next season with 5.5 million kg of that season's clip sold and no stockpile."
This should lead to better clearances at auction, higher prices for UK wool and reduced trading risk for the BWMB, putting it in its strongest selling position for a number of years, he added.
The Board had reached this position by extending its forward marketing system during 1996 which boosted sales.
"Because British wool is available and because manufacturers can commit themselves to forward purchases, British wool is used in preference to other wools," he stated.
Hartley said the increase in sales had not been achieved at the expense of price.
The UK auctions had been achieving consistently higher clearance rates than New Zealand (which produces similar types of wool) despite a close correlation in price movements over the year.
The BWMB was also hoping to introduce a new 12-month forward contract after consultations with wool users, he said. It expected to post reduced overall operating costs for 1996.
